idiom_name: single WSGI/ASGI callable + middleware chain (Django MIDDLEWARE)
implementation_notes: PEP 3333 makes the application a single callable (environ, start_response) invoked for every request and defines middleware as components that act as both application and server, so the front controller is that callable plus its wrapping layers; Django implements exactly this as one handler that builds the get_response chain from the MIDDLEWARE setting, with the view at the core of the onion. What replaces the classic structure: a callable plus a list of middleware factories replaces the FrontController class and its pre/post hooks, while decorators or FastAPI dependencies cover per-route concerns. The classic class form is only needed when no framework is acceptable.
code_sketch:
def application(environ, start_response):        # PEP 3333 entry point
    request = Request(environ)
    if not authenticate(request):                # shared behaviour
        return unauthorized(start_response)
    handler = ROUTES.match(request.method, request.path)   # dispatcher
    status, headers, body = handler(request)
    start_response(status, headers)
    return body

application = SessionMiddleware(AuthMiddleware(application))   # middleware chain
pitfalls: Middleware runs in list order on the way in and in reverse on the way out; authentication that needs the session must be listed after SessionMiddleware or it sees an anonymous user.
WSGI middleware must return an iterable body and call start_response exactly once - sync middleware wrapped around an ASGI app, or blocking I/O inside async views, stalls the loop.
Middleware must keep environ compliant when modifying the request, and streaming bodies must be closed; abandoned generators leak connections and file handles.
